decisions.reason: As a particle-therapy QA water phantom it serves a smaller niche and had a slower rollout, but it still aligns with the firm's high-end radiotherapy measurement strategy.
A small-volume ionization chamber is a core dosimetry product type with long clinical life cycles and strong fit with the firm's established QA portfolio.
Although it may overlap somewhat with other chamber models, it remains closely tied to the firm's core radiation measurement business and is unlikely to be withdrawn quickly.
A standard clinical ionization chamber is a staple product for radiotherapy QA, and firms in this market usually retain such validated devices for many years.
An ionization chamber for relative dosimetry supports routine clinical workflows central to the customer base, so it is likely to remain in the catalog.
Thimble ionization chambers are established workhorse devices in clinical dosimetry, with only a modest risk of rationalization if the portfolio becomes too crowded.
